    • allowedHosts

      public CsrfBoundary.Builder allowedHosts(String... values)
      The host names this server answers to. When set, every request, safe ones included, whose own host is not one of them is refused with 421 HOST_NOT_ALLOWED.

      Matching is case-insensitive and ignores the port. A trailing-dot variant is a different name. Replaces any earlier list. This is the DNS-rebinding control for applications served over plain HTTP.

      Parameters:
      values - Host names with no port, e.g. "app.example.com" or "[::1]". Must not be null, and no entry may be null or blank.
      Returns:
      This object.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If values or an entry is null, blank, or not a bare host.

    • trustedForwarding

      public CsrfBoundary.Builder trustedForwarding(CsrfBoundary.ForwardedSource value)
      Trusts the forwarded origin one proxy header family carries, for HTTP requests and WebSocket handshakes alike.

      With a source other than CsrfBoundary.ForwardedSource.NONE, the request's own origin is the forwarded host and proto of that one family, and nothing else: there is no fallback to Host or getScheme(), and X-Forwarded-Port is never read. A request missing either value, or with a malformed one, is refused with a FORWARDED_* reason. See trustedHops(int) for how an entry is selected.

      Turn this on only if every request reaches the server through a proxy that removes or appends after any client-supplied copy of the header. A server clients can reach directly lets them choose the origin. See also trustedProxies(String...) to believe only a listed peer address.

      Parameters:
      value - The source. Must not be null. Defaults to CsrfBoundary.ForwardedSource.NONE.
      Returns:
      This object.

    • trustedHops

      public CsrfBoundary.Builder trustedHops(int value)
      The number of proxies that append to the forwarded header.

      The entries of the header are counted in wire order across all its lines and commas, and the nth from the right is used; entries to its left are ignored. A chain of proxies that overwrite the header stays at 1. Never set this above the number of proxies that append: an overstated value selects an entry the client wrote, and that fails open. An understated value selects an inner hop and only causes refusals.

      Parameters:
      value - The hop count, 1 to 16. Defaults to 1.
      Returns:
      This object.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If value is outside 1 to 16.

    • trustedProxies

      public CsrfBoundary.Builder trustedProxies(String... cidrs)
      Believes the forwarded headers only from peers in these address ranges.

      Without this, trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource) believes the forwarded headers from whoever sends them. With it, the peer address the container reports (HTTP: ServletRequest.getRemoteAddr()) must be in a range. A request from another peer that carries a forwarded host in the selected family is refused (FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED); one that does not is judged on the container's own view, as if forwarding were off. A peer that cannot be parsed, or that the container did not report, is not trusted.

      Each entry is an IPv4 or IPv6 literal with an optional /prefix. Host bits are masked (10.0.0.1/8 is 10.0.0.0/8); /0 trusts every peer of its family. Names are never resolved, and a bracketed form, a zone id or an IPv4-mapped IPv6 form is refused (write the IPv4 form). An IPv4-mapped IPv6 peer is matched as the IPv4 address it carries.

      Use this only where the container reports the TCP peer: it is meaningless, or unsafe, where the container rewrites the peer from a header (Jetty's ForwardedRequestCustomizer, Tomcat's RemoteIpValve, the PROXY protocol). On WebSocket handshakes the peer comes from CsrfBoundary.checkHandshake(String, HandshakeHosts, Map, java.net.InetAddress); a container that supplies none (Tomcat) refuses every handshake that carries a forwarded host.

      Parameters:
      cidrs - The ranges. At least one; none may be null or invalid. Replaces any earlier list.
      Returns:
      This object.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If there are no ranges or one is invalid.
